title: First Steps
description: The floor is no longer enough. Standing between you and the warm light across the room is only the distance of your own two feet — and that distance feels infinite, terrifying, exhilarating. Someone is calling your name. You want to go to them. You are not sure your legs know how.

outcomes.narration: Your legs remember what your mind forgot — they know movement, they know urgency. The world blurs. Three steps, four, five — and then ground meets your knees, but you've laughing before the sting arrives. You've flown and landed and lived to laugh about it.

You launch forward with all your intent — and immediately everything is too fast. Your feet tangle, the floor rises to meet you, and the laugh becomes a cry. Someone runs to you. The light across the room can wait.

choices.label: Shuffle one careful step at a time

outcomes.narration: Left foot. Right foot. Left foot again. Each step is a small triumph, each balance point a tiny meditation. You cross the room in what feels like an hour but couldn't have been more than a minute. Someone claps. You did it slowly, and that is its own kind of brave.

You lower yourself to the floor with great dignity. Standing is a trap. Running is a trap. You will observe from here, thank you. The person calling your name laughs, and something about that laugh makes you reconsider — but not today.
